worst: B: Summary calls DRIFT a 'related 52-week trial' separate from the Annals trial, though matching 34% deficit design suggests they are the same trial
worst_summary_quote: A related 52-week trial (DRIFT, NCT03411356) was designed to address those gaps with objective adherence measures.
worst_page_quote: This 80% energy restriction on three fast days per week translates to a targeted weekly energy deficit of ~34%.
reader_gets_wrong: A reader would think the 12-month Annals result and DRIFT are two different trials, so the evidence base looks larger than one trial.
notes: Annals paper not in links. Reused PMC9421629 protocol (also as researchsquare rs-1663131 preprint), Medical Dialogues; clinicaltrials/scimex/newsweek/healthday unusable. Core result (7.6% vs 5%, 165 randomized, 80% on 3 days, 34.3% deficit) matches. Not in compared pages: 2.89 kg, n=84/81, 125 (76%) completers, no binge-eating, adherence claim (C, maybe from unfetched page). Omitted 58% vs 47% reaching 5% loss and 300 min/week exercise plus behavioral support in both arms (A). Opus summary hedges that full paper was not retrieved and that Newsweek ease claim is interpretation. Less misleading than Haiku round: does not say DRIFT is pending.
